message.content: Lions mate during the breeding season, which can occur year‑round but peaks in spring and summer. A male will approach a receptive female, often after establishing dominance over other males. He may scent‑mark the area with urine or feces to signal his presence. When the female is in estrus (lasting about 2–3 days), she will display a “standing heat” posture—standing upright with her tail raised and her hindquarters exposed. The male will mount her from behind, and copulation typically lasts only a few minutes. After mating, the male may guard the female to protect her from rival males. If successful, fertilization occurs internally, and the female will carry the pregnancy for about 110 days before giving birth.
